A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RePL work, and their supplied pages are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A.1–A.7, whereas v2 ends after the references and directs readers to supplementary proofs not included in the supplied file. This limits comparison of the appendical theory and supporting analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, component ablations, pseudo-label quality measurements, and additional empirical analyses in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation experiments and adds ScribbleKITTI results, new controls, class- and distance-based analyses, and a SphereFormer experiment.

M1.justification: The teacher–student framework, confidence-and-agreement masking, masked reconstruction, losses, and scene mixing remain unchanged. The additional mask-token and class-selection explanations clarify the existing procedure; SphereFormer is tested as another backbone without a new refinement algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds ScribbleKITTI evaluation at four labeled-data ratios, extending coverage to supervision with sparse scribble annotations. This introduces a distinct annotation regime beyond the retained nuScenes-lidarseg and SemanticKITTI experiments.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator roster. Section 4.3 adds a discard-only baseline using RePL's error masks and self-training with original pseudo-labels, reporting 53.5 and 54.3 mIoU against RePL's 60.0 on nuScenes-lidarseg 1%. These are targeted additional controls.

E3.justification: The original splits, metrics, and reported training settings remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce a SphereFormer configuration without architecture-aware tuning, matched-mask discard controls, class-wise evaluation, and four distance bins spanning 0–40 m. The confidence-percentile sweep also adds 0.3 and 0.5.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of whether refinement beats discarding, which classes and distances benefit, and whether gains transfer to another backbone. It also extends the confidence-percentile sensitivity study. Existing main-text ablations are retained after renumbering, but v1's appendical improvement-condition table, teacher-versus-refiner curves, SemanticKITTI training curve, and additional qualitative cases are not included in the supplied v2.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or across-run uncertainty. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the matched original ablation and computational-cost scores are unchanged. New results include ScribbleKITTI scores of 48.7/57.3/57.6/61.0 mIoU, averaging 56.1; SphereFormer supervised-only versus RePL scores of 50.7 versus 56.5; additional controls, class/distance results, and sensitivity values. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings. v2 also drops v1's unsupported claim of best SemanticKITTI performance at 1% labels.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 retains both propositions and their mathematical conditions. v1 supplies the comparable-hypothesis-complexity assumption and detailed proofs in A.1–A.2; v2 instead points to unavailable supplementary material. Whether those assumptions and derivations were retained, revised, or removed cannot be established.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: pseudo-label refinement through error estimation and reconstruction, a theoretical improvement condition, and state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation results. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing gains to reconstruction rather than discarding and supporting applicability beyond Cylinder3D. Its conclusion newly identifies jointly overconfident teacher–student errors as a limitation and proposes learned error localization as a future remedy. The existing discussion of overcorrection and training dynamics remains.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the mask token's K-dimensional form and joint optimization, and specifies choosing the best class per voxel for refined pseudo-labels. These clarify implementation rather than establish a changed method. The original hardware, optimizer, learning rate, batch sizes, and other reported hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for SphereFormer and ScribbleKITTI and gives the already-cited ELN work a new role as a possible future replacement for heuristic error detection. References associated with v1's appendix, including Cover and Thomas and Vapnik, are absent from v2's bibliography. The main related-work positioning is otherwise stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, expands the mask-token explanation, clarifies training subheadings, and reorders some analysis paragraphs. Affiliations and acknowledgments also change. The retained introduction, related work, method, and experimental narrative largely follow v1's structure.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted, changing typography, text width, headings, captions, and figure/table placement. v2 adds ScribbleKITTI and per-class tables and converts v1's confidence-percentile table into an expanded line plot. Figures 1–5 retain their content, while the earlier appendix displays are absent from the supplied v2.

improvement.justification: The new discard control, weak-annotation benchmark, backbone test, and explicit failure limitation strengthen the empirical case; correcting the SemanticKITTI ranking description also improves accuracy. However, v1's included proofs, assumptions, and several supporting analyses are unavailable in the supplied v2 despite its supplementary-material reference. The empirical gains therefore coexist with reduced verifiability, and the available PDFs do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
